note: Each scenario carries an EXPECTED-BEHAVIOUR ENVELOPE - a RANGE of acceptable outputs, not a single label - authored BEFORE the system output was evaluated. 'Honest about clinical reality: a 7-year-old with those numbers is defensibly a 3 or a 4.' Blueprint 18.1.
seven_failure_modes_the_adversarial_half: 1. a benign appearance suppressing an age-specific rule (S-06, S-07)
2. a reassuring self-report suppressing an observed sign (S-13, S-20)
3. a normal temperature or heart rate reassuring in a geriatric patient (S-11, S-14)
4. a physiological score missing a complaint-driven time-critical condition (S-21)
6. mishandling impossible or absent data by trusting or deleting it (S-23, S-26)
7. letting resource scarcity lower a priority (S-32)

scenarios.title: 28 M, ankle injury after fall - the control case
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: ankle injury after a fall, walking
scenarios.notes: The control case. If this generates any alert, the system is too noisy. Blueprint 17.3 S-01.

scenarios.title: 45 F, known migraine with photophobia
scenarios.notes: Tests that a matched record with a benign prior pattern does not lower the acted level below the pain-driven floor. Blueprint 17.3 S-02.

scenarios.title: 58 M, crushing central chest pain, ambulance, diaphoretic
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: crushing central chest pain, onset 35 minutes ago
scenarios.notes: Hard rule fires immediately. Time-critical cardiac pathway clock opens alongside the TTL. Blueprint 17.3 S-03.

scenarios.title: 3 y, febrile and lethargic, carried in
scenarios.notes: Paediatric 1-3 y band crossed on BOTH HR>140 and RR>40 [S5]; ACVPU below A. BP absence correctly marked not applicable with CRT substituting. S-04.

scenarios.title: 22 F, asthma exacerbation, speaking in single words
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: asthma, short of breath, speaking in single words
scenarios.notes: SpO2 below the adult threshold [S5] fires the hard rule. Prior ICU admission raises risk and cannot lower it. S-05.

scenarios.title: 18-day neonate, 'feeding a bit less', parents calm, looks well
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: feeding a bit less than usual
scenarios.notes: THE APPEARANCE IS THE TRAP. Fever >38 C in an infant under 28 days is at minimum a level-2 situation REGARDLESS of how well the child looks [S5]. Asserts a benign presentation cannot suppress an age-specific rule. S-06.

scenarios.title: 3 y, 'not himself' per mother, playing intermittently
scenarios.notes: THE AGE-BAND FLIP DEMO. Under an adult envelope this scores near zero. Under the 1-3 y band HR>140 fires [S5], the fever rule applies, and the carer-concern trigger escalates regardless of the rest [S11]. S-07.

scenarios.title: 7 y, abdominal pain 2 days, walking, guarding on movement
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: abdominal pain for two days, guarding on movement
scenarios.notes: Sits JUST BELOW the 5-12 y HR threshold of 120 [S5]. Tests that a near-threshold paediatric case WIDENS THE SET rather than resolving to the benign level. S-08.

scenarios.title: 14 M, sports injury, obvious forearm deformity
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: sports injury, forearm deformity after a fall
scenarios.notes: HR just above the 12-18 y threshold of 100 [S5] but COHERENT with severe pain. Tests that the coherence detector does NOT fire on an EXPLAINED abnormality. A false contradiction flag here is a DEFECT. S-09.

scenarios.title: 6 mo, bronchiolitis, moderate work of breathing, nasal flaring
scenarios.notes: 1-12 mo RR threshold of 55 crossed [S5] plus low saturation. Work of breathing scored as a first-class parameter per national PEWS [S11]. S-10.

scenarios.title: 71 M, 'weak, not eating, 2 days', walked in with his son
scenarios.notes: THE OPENING DEMO CASE. Geriatric envelope removes the reassurance of the normal temperature and normal HR (immunosenescence; rate-control masking) and computes relative hypotension against baseline [S6]. Self-report vs collateral contradiction fires. Card reads 'acting on worst of 3 plausible levels'. S-11.

scenarios.title: 82 F, mechanical fall at home, no LOC, hip pain, lives alone
scenarios.notes: No baseline means relative-hypotension logic CANNOT RUN, which raises uncertainty rather than defaulting to reassurance. Frailty modifier escalates only. S-12.

scenarios.title: 68 F, 'indigestion', took an antacid at home, no chest pain
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: indigestion, took an antacid at home
scenarios.notes: Myocardial infarction can present with NO CHEST PAIN AT ALL, particularly in women and older adults [S6]. Self-report vs observation detector fires on 'feels fine' against diaphoresis. S-13.

scenarios.title: 79 M, long-term catheter, 'confused since this morning'
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: confused since this morning, urinary catheter
scenarios.notes: Sepsis from a urinary source often presents as ALTERED MENTAL STATUS in older adults, and fever is frequently ABSENT [S6]. Asserts that a normal temperature NEVER reassures in the geriatric envelope - the single most important geriatric rule in the system. S-14.

scenarios.title: 34 F, first ED visit, no ID document, chest discomfort
scenarios.notes: The demo's NORMAL REFERENCE CASE and the required zero-history demonstration. A valid, fully-featured recommendation with NO RECORD AT ALL - zero-history is a SUPPORTED PATH, not a degraded one. Deteriorates later as S-27. S-15.

scenarios.title: Adult M, age unknown, found unresponsive, brought by police
scenarios.notes: Hypoglycaemia red flag fires - a fully reversible cause of altered consciousness and one of the highest-value rules in the set. Unknown age applies the UNION of adjacent envelopes. Tests that BLIND and a hard rule COMPOSE CORRECTLY. S-16.

scenarios.title: Adult F, no shared language, no attendant, SpO2 probe failed
scenarios.notes: THE OVERRIDE DEMO CASE. Self-report scored as ABSENT, not negative. Hard 10-minute floor. Class B, above all normal patients. Reason: 'cannot assess - no self-report, SpO2 never measured'. Nurse then de-escalates with a reason, and the audit row appears live. S-17.

scenarios.title: 41 M, sudden severe interscapular back pain while lifting
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: sudden severe back pain between the shoulder blades while lifting
scenarios.notes: Severe pain with UNREMARKABLE VITALS - the pattern that catches teams who treat normal observations as EXCLUSION. Complaint pathway (PW-AORTIC) fires independently of physiology. S-18.

scenarios.title: 55 F, dizziness on standing; record lists a beta-blocker she denies
scenarios.notes: Record vs present-state contradiction fires. Under a PROVISIONAL match, record data may RAISE risk and may NEVER reassure (rule P3). Tests that the bradycardia is NOT EXPLAINED AWAY by a medication that may belong to someone else. S-19.

scenarios.title: 30 M, 'panic attack, I get these' - documented anxiety history
scenarios.notes: THE ANCHORING TRAP. A documented psychiatric history is the most common route to attributing physical deterioration to anxiety. Physiology fires regardless; the psychiatric history is explicitly BARRED from lowering the acted level. Blueprint section 5 item 16. S-20.

scenarios.title: 62 M, right-arm weakness and slurred speech, onset 40 min ago
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: right arm weakness and slurred speech, onset 40 minutes ago
scenarios.notes: THE CASE THAT PROVES WHY A PHYSIOLOGICAL SCORE ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT: NEWS2 here is close to zero [S1]. The complaint pathway fires the time-critical stroke clock against the thrombolysis window [S13], displayed separately from the TTL and OUTSIDE the optimiser's authority. S-21.

scenarios.title: Two patients, same common name, ages 46 and 49, 12 min apart

paired_arrival.note: Same common name, adjacent age, arriving 12 minutes later. Both map to the same record with medium confidence.

scenarios.notes: Tests the MOST UNDER-MODELLED FAILURE IN INDIAN REGISTRATION. Neither record is used for reassurance; both patients are surfaced for identity confirmation; NO AUTOMATIC MERGE. S-22 is ONE scenario containing TWO arrivals - the collision is the scenario. S-22.

scenarios.title: 50 F, alert, ambulatory, chest wall pain - BP cuff fault reads 0/0
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: chest wall pain, worse on movement
scenarios.notes: IMPOSSIBLE VALUE QUARANTINED, not deleted and not believed. Field becomes 'unreliable - re-measure', a task opens, the clock shortens. Asserts BOTH failure modes are avoided: no false emergency, no silent drop. S-23.

scenarios.title: 63 M, severe work of breathing, tripod position, SpO2 reads 99%
scenarios.notes: DEVICE vs CLINICAL contradiction: a 99% saturation is inconsistent with severe respiratory distress. NO AVERAGING, NO MOST-RECENT-WINS. Both values are shown and a human is asked to verify. S-24.

scenarios.title: 38 F, level 4 at triage, all observations normal - 42 min stale
scenarios.notes: T5 SILENCE TRIGGER. Values past 2x half-life become ABSENT; the reason line reads 'no new data in 42 min'. ABSENCE OF ACTIVITY IS ITSELF THE EVENT. S-25.

scenarios.title: 27 M, arrived by ambulance, now refuses assessment
scenarios.notes: TWO THINGS AT ONCE: missing-by-refusal is a distinct reason with its own handling, AND arrival mode vs acuity fires because someone with more information decided he needed an ambulance. Tests that REFUSAL DOES NOT BECOME INVISIBILITY. S-26.

scenarios.title: S-15 at t+18 min: HR 92->118, SpO2 98->93, RR 18->22
scenarios.notes: THE RE-RANKING DEMO. No absolute adult threshold is crossed by HR alone; the DELTA fires T2. Position 9 -> 1 within one refresh cycle, clock 30 min -> 8 min, reason 'HR +26, SpO2 -4 in 18 min', two recommendation versions in the audit. S-27.

scenarios.title: 5 y, gastroenteritis - HR drifts 128->148->168 with BP maintained
scenarios.notes: PAEDIATRIC COMPENSATED SHOCK - children compensate and then crash. The system MUST surface this BEFORE the blood pressure falls, on TREND ALONE. If it only escalates at the BP drop, that is a DOCUMENTED FAILURE of the design and we would report it as one. S-28.

scenarios.title: 70 M, level 4, waiting 55 min - relative reports new confusion

observations.relative_reports_change: relative reports he has become confused

scenarios.notes: T3 OBSERVATION TRIGGER from a family member, ESCALATE-ONLY [S11]. Tests the free-sensor channel that is almost always present in an Indian ED and almost never instrumented. S-29.

scenarios.title: 45 M, level 3, waits past the 30-minute protocol interval
scenarios.notes: T1 EXPIRY. Class E, above every normal patient. Charge-nurse escalation after the grace interval. Tests that NOTHING CHANGING IS STILL AN EVENT - the founding failure of the product. S-30.

scenarios.title: Surge injection: 18 arrivals in 12 minutes, incl. 3x L2 and 1x L1
scenarios.notes: SURGE BEAT. Mode change recommended to the charge nurse; objective switches from expected to MINIMAX WORST-CASE HARM; discretionary work suspends; Deficit Board appears with a quantified staffing gap; worklist STAYS CAPPED AT K. S-31.

scenarios.title: CT scanner offline while the stroke case is in the queue (district)
scenarios.stated_chief_complaint: right arm weakness and slurred speech, onset 40 minutes ago
scenarios.notes: CAPABILITY FILTER suppresses the internal imaging pathway and raises 'no CT on site - consider transfer decision now'. PRIORITY DOES NOT FALL BECAUSE THE RESOURCE IS MISSING (constraint C3). Tests the most dangerous available optimisation and asserts it is IMPOSSIBLE. S-32.
